name: global-memory
description: Adds a machine-wide memory folder beside the per-project auto memory, so facts about the machine reach every session from any folder: rewrites the memory section for both folders and loads the global MEMORY.md. With an ai-memory wiki, it adds the pages that match each request.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Add the machine-wide memory folder to every session. Off, the memory section stays as Claude Code wrote it.

globalDir.title: Global memory folder
globalDir.description: Folder of the machine-wide memory, with its own MEMORY.md. It can be a folder in a git repo, to version the memories. A leading ~ is your home folder.

wikiDir.title: ai-memory wiki folder
wikiDir.description: Wiki folder of an ai-memory server (github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory), such as ~/.local/share/ai-memory/wiki. Set, the global index comes from the _rules/indice-memorias.md page of the wiki's _global project, and the project index from the same page of the project named like the folder the project memory links to. A missing page falls back to MEMORY.md.

recall.title: Recall
recall.description: With wikiDir set, search the ai-memory wiki for the words of each request and add the best matching pages to it, whole, within recallMaxTokens. No model is called. A pasted agent message, a scheduled prompt or a prompt of under two subject words searches nothing.

recallMaxTokens.title: Recall budget
recallMaxTokens.description: Most tokens recall adds to one request, estimated at 2 characters per token. Up to 3 pages go in, each whole; a page already added in this conversation is not added again.

aiMemoryCommand.title: ai-memory command
aiMemoryCommand.description: The ai-memory CLI that recall runs (ai-memory call memory_query). A leading ~ is your home folder.
